pins.definition: To contact someone or a place by telephone.
To use a telephone to contact someone.

situation: A woman stands in her kitchen holding an old rotary telephone to her ear.
subject: the telephone call
brief: A woman in a retro-futuristic kitchen presses a glowing orange landline handset to her ear, while thin, luminous soundwave rings ripple visibly through the air from the mouthpiece toward the wall. The rotary dial on the turquoise phone is lit from within, casting a warm orange glow across her face.
prompt: A woman in a retro-futuristic kitchen presses a glowing orange landline handset to her ear, while thin, luminous soundwave rings ripple visibly through the air from the mouthpiece toward the wall. The rotary dial on the turquoise phone is lit from within, casting a warm orange glow across her face. a 1970s science-fiction paperback cover, airbrushed gradients, a muted offset-print palette with visible halftone, dramatic scale and a confident optimistic mood. It renders an ordinary modern scene as though it were the future someone once imagined, so it suits machinery, travel, work and plans as readily as spacecraft. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
